reason: I tried to break this one hardest, because the form that circulates has a comma after 'head' ('make a battering-ram of my head, and make a way through this rough-and-tumble world'), and the proposal drops it. The proposal is right. I downloaded the Internet Archive full text of Cheney's Roberts Brothers edition (louisamayalcotth00alcouoft) and read the passage: 'I can't do much with my hands ; so I will make a battering-ram of my head and make a way through this rough-and-tumble world.' No comma after 'head'. The semicolon after 'hands' is Cheney's. The locator checks out at every level. The letter is headed 'To her Father, written from Mrs. Reed's. BOSTON, Nov. 29, 1856.' The running heads bracket the sentence between 'Authorship. 89' and '90 Louisa May Alcott.', so it is on page 89, not 88 or 90. The chapter heading index gives 'V. AUTHORSHIP 75', and CHAPTER V opens with the word AUTHORSHIP, so chapter five is right. The birthday reading is right too: the letter says 'for birthdays are dismal times to me' and 'with the birthday pin upon my bosom', and Alcott was born 29 November 1832, so this is her twenty-fourth. The verifier's correction away from a journal entry of 1850 is therefore sound, and the retag from Diary to Correspondence is sound, since Cheney prints journal and letter material side by side and the surrounding text is a run of December 1856 journal entries, which is exactly how a letter gets mistaken for a journal here. Mechanics pass: source line 127 characters, leads with the name, no dash, curly quotes only, ends in a full stop, in scope, publishable, nothing shipped, no near match, Alcott at one of three for the year with her other line in month 5, so no month collision.
